findings.what: No test checks that the black set is sorted before use. The test 'frozen black, tau and population are read, not written, and black is used sorted' passes black [2, 0] on A3. On that sub-board (two separate nodes) the order makes no difference. If the sort is removed from checkDiagram, all 111 P6-A1 tests still pass, yet e6(-26) given its black positions in reverse is then judged not admissible. The real code is correct; only the test is missing.
findings.evidence: python3 scratchpad/p6-a1-review/mutants.py <root> on the mutant 'return [...black];' gives Tests 111 passed (111). python3 apply_and_run.py with observe.mjs under the same mutant: E6 black [4,3,2,1] with identity tau gives admissible false, condition_3 {nodes:[0,5], value:'-7/2; -25/12'}, and satake throws 'NotAdmissible: not admissible: condition_3'; B3 black [2,1] gives not-an-integer '-19/10'. The unmutated engine on both diagrams: admissible true, dim_k 52, A2
findings.specRef: P6-A1 instruction 5.2 ('d.black is used sorted (the oracle sorts X)'); E-5; COMMON 4.3 ('A test must fail when the behaviour it guards is removed')
findings.proposedFix: Add a test that calls admissibility and satake on E6 with black [4,3,2,1] (and on B3 with [2,1]) and expects results equal to those for the sorted list.

findings.what: The planned node lists for not-a-symmetry and not-an-involution are only tested on cases where other readings give the same nodes. Two mutants survive: building not-a-symmetry nodes from columns instead of rows, and building not-an-involution nodes from every position tau moves. The readings differ on non-symmetric boards and on permutations of rank 5 or more. The engine itself follows the planned readings: 0 disagreements with an independent computation over 18456 such cases.
findings.evidence: mutants.py: 'symmetry nodes by column instead of row' and 'not-an-involution nodes: every moved position' give Tests 111 passed (111). python3 rowcol.py: B3 tau [2,1,0] gives rows [0,2] and columns [1]; C3 tau [2,1,0] gives rows [1] and columns [0,2]; B4 has 6 such permutations and F4 has 2. A5 tau [1,2,0,4,3] moves {0..4}, but tau(tau(i)) != i only on {0,1,2}
findings.specRef: SPEC 5.2 Reason; P6-A1 instruction 5.5 table (plan readings); COMMON 4.3
findings.proposedFix: Add reasons.test cases B3 flip ({code:'not-a-symmetry', nodes:[0,2]}) and A5 [1,2,0,4,3] ({code:'not-an-involution', nodes:[0,1,2]}).

findings.what: A population with a hole in it gets through the input check without a RangeError. checkPopulation uses Array.prototype.map, which skips holes. As a result theta returns NaN and shadow2 returns a sparse array. A population with an explicit undefined entry is correctly refused.
findings.evidence: node --import register.mjs holes.mjs <root>: theta(A3 split, [1, <hole>, 0]) = [ -1, NaN, 0 ]; shadow2 = [ 2, <1 empty item>, 0 ]; theta(..., [1, undefined, 0]) throws 'RangeError: the entry undefined of the population is not an integer'
findings.specRef: P6-A1 instruction 5.2 'Malformed input (plan)'; decisions/P6-A1.md 'a population ... with a non-integer entry' gives RangeError
findings.proposedFix: Validate with an index loop (for k < n, read p[k]) or with Array.from(p) before mapping, so that a hole reaches the Number.isInteger check.

findings.what: Property 9 does not check every catalogue record of the drawn board. Each run picks one record at random. With the recorded seed, 20 of the 167 records are never drawn by 'theta is an involution' and 56 are never drawn by 'theta permutes the roots'. This is partly covered elsewhere, because satake() asserts both facts for all 167 records in p6a-satake-computed.
findings.evidence: node p9coverage.mjs <root> (fc.assert with seed 20261025 and the test's arbitraries): involution: 400 runs, 147 of 167 records drawn, never drawn include A8 sl(9,R), B8 so(17), D6 so*(12), D8 so(7,9) and others; permutes roots: 200 runs, 111 of 167 drawn, 56 never drawn
findings.specRef: SPEC 5.7 property 9 ('theta(theta(p)) = p for every catalogue record of B, and theta permutes the roots')
findings.proposedFix: Draw B and p as now, then loop over all records of B inside the property instead of drawing an index k.

findings.what: The open question on boards in several pieces was not settled. The guard admits a board made of finite pieces, but satake on many admissible pairs there throws a plain EngineError from classifyRestricted, which is not one of the E-10 classes. Examples are the split forms of A1+A1 and A2+A2. The oracle raises ValueError on the same pairs, so the agent's choice matches the oracle and contradicts the plan's sentence 'restricted_board null'. The MERGE entry rules on coverage and check order but not on this point. The guarded identify call and the labels 1..m path of E-7 are untested; the instruction said not to pin them, and the two mutants survive.
findings.evidence: compare.mjs: 26 admissible pairs on A1+A1, A2+A2, A1+A2, B2+A1, A3+A3 and G2+G2 throw in both oracle and engine, e.g. 'EngineError: classifyRestricted: unrecognised simply-laced system (r, N) = (4, 12)' for A2+A2 split. restrictedBoard on those 26 matches the oracle (labels 1..m, no name). mutants.py: 'identify ... without the connectedness guard' and 'labels empty when no name' give 111 passed
findings.specRef: E-10; E-7 row 'restricted board'; SPEC 5.6; P6-A1 instruction trap 22
findings.proposedFix: MERGE decides: either satake throws NeedsConnectedBoard (E-10) on a board in pieces, or the EngineError is documented as intended. Then pin the chosen behaviour, and restrictedBoard's labels 1..m, in one test.

checked: 1. Engine against oracle (scratchpad/p6-a1-review/oracle_dump.py and compare.mjs). theta: 4000 random populations in [-9,9], 0 disagreements. shadow2: 4000, 0 disagreements. Boards: the 32 named types, 7 renumbered (Big) boards and 6 direct sums; tau ranged over involutions, all symmetries and arbitrary permutations. admissibility: 22834 pairs, 0 disagreements in verdicts and Reason records. Of these, 4378 use involutive symmetries over all subsets of every board up to rank 8. The other 18456 cover all permutations up to rank 4, all symmetries, and 6 random non-symmetries per larger board. satake: 241 admissible pairs x 19 fields, 0 disagreements; the other 26 pairs (boards in pieces) throw in both. Golden: all 167 records x 19 computed fields, 0 disagreements, with the C2 exception for the four records. The 7 admissible pairs that are not records are included. The oracle's admissible pairs equal golden admissible_pairs (174). restrictedBoard: 267 pairs; orbits, doubled simple roots, Cartan matrix, composite words, name and labels all agree; reduced lengths agree on 241.

2. Reason records. Codes produced across the 22834 pairs: not-a-symmetry 18232, not-an-involution 16800, moves-black-set 2128, differs-from-minus-wX 20793, not-an-integer 5685. Nodes are positions and value is the oracle's fraction text, joined by '; ' when several nodes fail. There are 1539 such cases, 594 with different fractions; 534 of these are on named boards with involutive tau, the plan's figure. E-7: 52 labelled finite boards (sub-boards of affine and twisted boards, labels containing 0, and A5 on positions 2,3,4). 6280 diagrams x 4 functions give results identical to unlabelled copies. The planned readings in reasonConventions fit SPEC 5.2 and 2.15. The single-value contract versus the '; ' format is still open (see notes).

3. Guards. 22 boards x 5 functions all throw the right class, each also an EngineError: 4 one-way boards (one is a one-way piece beside A1) give NeedsTwoWayRoads; 13 affine, twisted and cycle boards, 2 indefinite boards, 2 finite+affine sums and A2~ with black nodes give NotFiniteType. Malformed diagrams: 19 shapes x 5 functions throw RangeError, except a missing or null board, which gives TypeError (note). Populations: 11 malformed forms checked; only a hole slips through (finding). NotAdmissible: 6 pairs x {satake, restrictedBoard} carry data deep-equal to admissibility(d), with name and message 'not admissible: <first failed key>'. A2+A2 split confirmed: the oracle raises in classify_restricted; the engine throws EngineError; restrictedBoard gives labels [1..4] and no name.

4. Tests. npm test -w packages/engine: 81 files, 2530 tests passed. tsc --noEmit -p packages/engine: exit 0. site scripts.test.ts (clock guard): 20 passed. 27 mutants of my own: 19 killed and 8 survive. 3 survivors are equivalent (simple root from the largest node, orbit unsorted, requireGcm dropped). 2 survivors are the disconnected-board paths the instruction leaves unpinned. 3 are test gaps (findings 1 and 2). The golden tests compare every computed field under rules 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7: Object.keys equality, labels() conversion, intEq, the C2 exception, and admissible_pairs as a set. satake_examples verdicts and key order are compared; real_forms is deferred to P6-A2's p6b-match. No golden value is typed into src. Tests type only values named in SPEC (A.5, 2.15 table, e6(-26)) or in the instruction (e6(-14)). The coverage split in the MERGE entry is sound: P6-A2's full-record test goes through satakeRecord to satake.

5. Purity: 138 diagrams x 5 functions leave black, tau, population and board unchanged; results share no arrays across calls. Named boards stay SafeInt; -0 never appears in 8000 outputs. No count in the results can be large (dim_g at most 248). No clock is read in the P6-A1 parallel files (grep). Bench (test/bench/p6a-satake.bench.ts, load average 3.6, 4 CPUs): satake medians from 2.52 ms (e7(-25)) to 7.65 ms (e8(8)), restrictedBoard 0.33 to 1.35 ms. This matches the report's 2.02 to 7.48 ms.
notes: No blocker and no major. Every computed value agrees with the oracle and the golden file on every case run. The findings are test gaps, one edge case in input checking, and one open question MERGE has not ruled on.

The MERGE entry rules on 2 of the agent's 6 open questions (coverage, check order). Still not ruled on: the '; ' format of not-an-integer when several nodes fail (SPEC 5.2 says 'the fraction'); the planned nodes of not-a-symmetry, not-an-involution and moves-black-set; the empty restricted board of a compact form; boards in pieces (finding 5).
satake_examples is now registered in coverage.json, but its real_forms field is not compared until P6-A2's p6b-match.test.ts lands. The gate cannot notice if that check is never written.

7 of the 135 restricted boards carry a name ('B2' or 'F4') while their cartan stays in orbit order, so cartanNumbers(rb.board) differs from cartan(rb.board.name). The records are su(2,2), sp(4,R), sp(2,2), so*(8), e6(-14), e6(2) and e8(-24). This follows the plan and P4-A1's folded board, but it contradicts the comment at board.ts:292. T13 must lay the board out by labels, not by name. classify, identify, gram, choleskyBasis, positiveRoots, longestWord and play all accept the restricted board objects (135 checked).

Hand-built Big boards are computed on a private SafeInt copy. A bigint population beyond 2^53 therefore throws EngineOverflow where Big arithmetic would succeed. The contract types results as number[], and decisions/P6-A1.md records this choice.
